'''James Wynne Dungey''' (1923–2015)<ref name=bio>{{Cite journal|last=Southwood|first=D. J.|date=October 2015|title=James Wynne Dungey 1923–2015|url=https://academic.oup.com/astrogeo/article/56/5/5.8/235460|journal=Astronomy and Geophysics|volume=56|issue=5|pages=5.8|doi=10.1093/astrogeo/atv162|doi-access=free|hdl=10044/1/29102|hdl-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> was a British space scientist who was pivotal in establishing the field of [[space weather]] and made significant contributions to the fundamental understanding of [[plasma physics]].

== Early life and education ==
Dungey grew up in [[Stamford, Lincolnshire]], the son of a schoolteacher. During [[World War II]], he worked at [[British Thomson-Houston|British Thompson-Houston]] in Rugby, on developments for [[radar]]. After the end of the war, he gained a degree in 1947 from [[Magdalene College, Cambridge]], part of the [[University of Cambridge]]. He then completed a Ph.D. at the same institution, under the supervision of [[Fred Hoyle]].<ref name=bio/>

==Career and research==
From 1950 to 1953 Dungey worked at the [[University of Sydney]] with [[Ron Giovanelli]], from 1953 to 1954 at [[Pennsylvania State University]], and from 1954 to 1957 back at the University of Cambridge. From 1957 to 1959 he was a mathematics lecturer at [[King's College, Newcastle upon Tyne]] (now Newcastle University) and from 1959 to 1963 he worked at the UK [[Atomic Weapons Establishment]]. In 1963 he moved to the [[Blackett Laboratory]] of [[Imperial College London]], where he was a physics professor from 1965 to until his retirement in 1984.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Stern|first=D.|date=December 1986|title=A conversation with Jim Dungey|url=https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1029/EO067i051p01394|journal=Eos, Transactions American Geophysical Union |volume=67 |issue=51 |pages=1394–1395 |doi=10.1029/eo067i051p01394 |bibcode=1986EOSTr..67.1394S|issn=0096-3941|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Southwood|first=D. J.|date=February 2016|title=James Wynne Dungey (1923–2015)|url=http://eos.org/articles/james-wynne-dungey-1923-2015 |journal=Eos, Transactions American Geophysical Union |volume=97 |doi=10.1029/2016EO044731|doi-access=free}}</ref>

=== The discovery of magnetic reconnection ===
Dungey introduced the concept of [[magnetic reconnection]], a mechanism that was not initially accepted but is now recognized to be of fundamental importance in all areas of [[Plasma (physics)|plasma]] (ionized gas) physics. Magnetic reconnection has key effects on astrophysical, space, and laboratory plasmas in converting magnetic energy into heat and energised charged particles. It also enables a wide range of phenomena by reconfiguring magnetic field lines. Reconnection is a process that occurs in the solar corona, interplanetary space, Earth's magnetosphere, fusion tokamaks and many astrophysical objects. It is also the key controlling factor in [[space weather]] effects on operational systems, causing the release of energy in [[solar flares]] and [[coronal mass ejection]]s  (CMEs) and being the key mechanism that transfers energy from the [[solar wind]] flow (and its enhancement due to CMEs) to Earth's space environment, the [[magnetosphere]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last=Lockwood|first=M.|date=June 2016|title=Jim Dungey, The Open Magnetosphere, and Space Weather|journal=Space Weather|volume=14|issue=6|pages=380–383|doi=10.1002/2016sw001438|bibcode=2016SpWea..14..380L|issn=1542-7390|doi-access=free}}</ref> It is also very important in fusion research, causing problems for the [[Magnetic confinement fusion|magnetic confinement]] of the plasma in [[tokamak]]s but is harnessed in some devices to help compress the plasma.

Dungey considered the origins of the known system of currents in the polar ionospheres detected using high-latitude magnetometers.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Dungey|first=J. W.|date=January 1961|title=Interplanetary Magnetic Field and the Auroral Zones|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.6.47|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=6|issue=2|pages=47–48|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.6.47|bibcode=1961PhRvL...6...47D|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He had been steered toward this work by his PhD supervisor, [[Fred Hoyle]], after Hoyle examined the DSc thesis of [[Ron Giovanelli]] in Sydney, Australia—a thesis that contained the concept of magnetic nulls acting to power solar flares by annihilating oppositely-directed magnetic fields at current sheets. Hoyle wondered if some such mechanism could power Earth's aurora. Dungey's innovations were to restrict the region of magnetic interaction in the current sheet and predict the magnetic field topology changes: this allowed energised particles and reconnected magnetic flux to escape along the current sheet<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Cowley|first=S. W. H. |date=February 2016|title=Hoyle and the magnetosphere|journal=Astronomy & Geophysics|language=en|volume=57|issue=1|pages=1.12|doi=10.1093/astrogeo/atw033|issn=1366-8781|doi-access=free|hdl=2381/37367|hdl-access=free}}</ref>

=== Initial reaction and acceptance of reconnection ===
Dungey initially had difficulty in getting his work published.  The most important journal for British [[space physics]] research at the time was [[Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society]] but his submission there was rejected. On the advice of [[Sydney Chapman (mathematician)|Sydney Chapman]] he submitted the work to [[Philosophical Magazine]], where it was finally accepted.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last=Dungey|first=J. W.|date=July 1953 |title=LXXVI. Conditions for the occurrence of electrical discharges in astrophysical systems|journal=The London, Edinburgh, and Dublin Philosophical Magazine and Journal of Science|volume=44|issue=354|pages=725–738|doi=10.1080/14786440708521050|issn=1941-5982}}</ref> There were technical problems with the mechanism that needed to be overcome. For example the initial theory of Parker and Sweet,<ref>{{Cite journal |title=1958IAUS....6..123S Page 123 |url=https://adsabs.harvard.edu/full/1958IAUS....6..123S |access-date=2022-02-26 |journal=Electromagnetic Phenomena in Cosmical Physics|bibcode=1958IAUS....6..123S |last1=Sweet |first1=P. A. |year=1958 |volume=6 |page=123 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Parker |first=E. N. |date=December 1957 |title=Sweet's mechanism for merging magnetic fields in conducting fluids |url=https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1029/JZ062i004p00509 |journal=Journal of Geophysical Research |volume=62 |issue=4 |pages=509–520 |doi=10.1029/jz062i004p00509 |bibcode=1957JGR....62..509P |issn=0148-0227|url-access=subscription }}</ref> although giving magnetic reconnection, is not fast enough and could not deliver enough voltage (which, by [[Faraday's law of induction|Faraday's law]], equals flux magnetic transfer rate). This was solved by aerodynamicist Harry Petschek<ref>{{Cite journal |title=1964NASSP..50..425P Page 425 |url=https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/full/1964NASSP..50..425P |access-date=2022-02-26 |journal=NASA Special Publication|bibcode=1964NASSP..50..425P |last1=Petschek |first1=H. E. |year=1964 |volume=50 |page=425 }}</ref> who added shock fronts standing on the inflow to the reconnection site: these have a number of effects but crucially open up the outflow region to allow more rapid ejection of reconnected flux and plasma along the current sheet, that being the limitation to Parker-Sweet reconnection and the cause of the choking-off of magnetic annihilation. Now it is recognised that the same role is played by [[Alfvén wave]]s.

In addition to this valid problem which needed to be overcome, a great many spurious problems were raised: for example, the inappropriate application of "[[Lenz's law]]" (a problem Dungey was aware of and had solved in his PhD work) and unnecessary philosophical objections to the concept of moving magnetic field lines. Dungey's 1961 paper described what came to be called the "open magnetosphere model" and only shortly preceded the advent of in-situ measurements by spacecraft. As more space data were accrued, the longer the list grew of features of magnetospheric and ionospheric structure and behaviour that were  uniquely explained by his idea.<ref name=":6">{{Cite book |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-319-18359-6 |title=Magnetospheric Plasma Physics: The Impact of Jim Dungey's Research |date=2015 |publisher=Springer International Publishing |isbn=978-3-319-18358-9 |editor-last=Cowley |editor-first=S. W. H. |series=Astrophysics and Space Science Proceedings |volume=41 |location=Cham |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-18359-6 |editor-last2=Southwood |editor-first2=D. J. |editor-last3=Mitton |editor-first3=S.}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{Cite journal |last=Cowley |first=S. W. H. |date=November 2019 |title=Brief Portrait of the Scientist as a Young Man: Researches on Dungey's "Open" Magnetosphere From the 1960s to the 1980s |journal=Journal of Geophysical Research: Space Physics |language=en |volume=124 |issue=11 |pages=8352–8360 |doi=10.1029/2019JA027507 |bibcode=2019JGRA..124.8352C |s2cid=210258606 |issn=2169-9380|doi-access=free }}</ref> Nevertheless, ironically, acceptance of the concept was more universal in areas away from magnetospheric physics, such as solar physics, astrophysics and laboratory plasma physics (including fusion research).<ref name=":3" /> In particular, Nobel laureate [[Hannes Alfvén]] was a vocal, trenchant and influential critic, rejecting reconnection along with his own (and now almost universally-used) concept of frozen-in magnetic flux for large-scale plasmas (also called "[[Alfvén's theorem]]" or "ideal MHD"),<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Alfvén |first=H. |date=August 1976 |title=On frozen-in field lines and field-line reconnection |journal=Journal of Geophysical Research |language=en |volume=81 |issue=22 |pages=4019–4021 |doi=10.1029/JA081i022p04019|bibcode=1976JGR....81.4019A }}</ref> which was part of the formulation of [[magnetohydrodynamics]] (MHD) for which he gained the [[Nobel Prize|Nobel prize]] in 1970. Reconnection is a breakdown of ideal MHD that occurs in thin current sheets and provides the solution to one of the biggest objections to ideal MHD by untangling field lines that would otherwise be ever more tangled by plasma velocity shears and vortices if frozen-in applied without it. Today, reconnection is well established as a key mechanism which is vital in explaining the transfer of mass, energy and momentum from the solar wind to the magnetosphere, thereby driving terrestrial space weather and geomagnetic disturbance.<ref name=":3" />

The circulation of plasma in the magnetosphere caused by reconnection is called "convection" and often referred to as the [[Dungey Cycle]]. Dungey envisaged this as a steady circulation with electric fields mapping throughout the magnetosphere (as predicted by Faraday's law for steady state); however, imbalances in the reconnection voltages in the dayside magnetopause and in the nightside tail current sheet were later recognised as the source of the phenomenon of the auroral [[substorm]] cycle.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=McPherron |first=R.L. |date=June 1979 |title=Magnetospheric substorms |url= |journal=Reviews of Geophysics |language=en |volume=17 |issue=4 |pages=657–681 |doi=10.1029/RG017i004p00657 |bibcode=1979RvGSP..17..657M }}</ref> The convection circulation in the ionosphere and magnetosphere for these non-steady conditions is explained by the "expanding contracting polar cap" (ECPC) model and the [[Dungey Cycle]] is understood in terms of the plasma (and frozen-in field) motions returning the magnetosphere-ionosphere system towards equilibrium after it has been perturbed by the dayside and/or tail reconnection.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cowley |first1=S.W.H |last2=Lockwood |first2=M. |date=1992 |title=Excitation and decay of solar-wind driven flows in the magnetosphere-ionosphere system |url=http://www.personal.reading.ac.uk/~ym901336/pdfs/92_CowleyandLockwood_1992.pdf |journal=Annales Geophysicae |language=en |volume=10 |issue=1–2 |pages=103–115 |bibcode=1992AnGeo..10..103C |issn=0992-7689}}</ref>

=== Later life ===
The citation for the award of Honorary Membership of the European Geophysical Society (now the [[European Geosciences Union]]) in 1994 emphasised the importance and breadth of Dungey's work both as a scientist and in training later generations.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=EGS Honorary Membership 1994 |url=https://www.egu.eu/egs/medalists/dungley94.htm |access-date=2022-02-26 |website=www.egu.eu}}</ref>

A great many features of Earth's [[magnetosphere]]  were first proposed and investigated by Dungey after he had proposed magnetic reconnection. He was the first to compute the length of the geomagnetic tail<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dungey |first=J. W. |date=April 1965 |title=The length of the magnetospheric tail |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1029/JZ070i007p01753 |journal=Journal of Geophysical Research |language=en |volume=70 |issue=7 |page=1753 |doi=10.1029/JZ070i007p01753|bibcode=1965JGR....70.1753D |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and his value was in good agreement with that found by the first spacecraft missions to visit that region of space.<ref>{{Cite encyclopedia |author-last= Hughes |author-first= J.W.  |title= The magnetopause, magnetotail, and magnetic reconnection |pages= 227–285 |encyclopedia=Introduction to Space Physics |date= 1995 |publisher=Cambridge University press |isbn=0-521-45104-3 |editor-last1=Kivelson |editor-first1=M. G. |editor-last2=Russell |editor-first2=C. T.  |location=Cambridge U.K.}}</ref> He predicted "lobe reconnection" when the [[interplanetary magnetic field]] points northward,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Dungey |first=J. W. |title=The structure of the exosphere of adventures in velocity space, in Geophysics, The Earth's Environment, Ed. C. DeWitt, J. Hieblot, and A. Lebeau |publisher=Gordon and Breach |year=1963 |location=New York |pages=505–550}}</ref> which is observed by low-Earth orbit spacecraft (for example during the [[Space hurricane]] event) and in observations of dayside auroral forms.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lockwood |first1=M. |last2=Moen |first2=J. I. |date=August 1999 |title= Reconfiguration and closure of lobe flux by reconnection during northward IMF: possible evidence for signatures in cusp/cleft auroral emissions |url=https://centaur.reading.ac.uk/38744/ |journal=Annales Geophysicae|language=en |volume=17 |issue=8 |pages=996–1011 |issn=0992-7689 |doi=10.1007/s00585-999-0996-2|bibcode=1999AnGeo..17..996L |s2cid=11653923 |doi-access=free }}</ref> Lobe reconnection has the important implication that the magnetosphere is rarely, if ever, an equilibrium system.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lockwood |first=M. |date=February 2022 |title=The Joined-up Magnetosphere |journal=Frontiers in Astronomy and Space Sciences |language=en |volume=9 |article-number= 856188 |doi=10.3389/fspas.2022.856188|bibcode=2022FrASS...956188L |doi-access=free }}</ref> Dungey was the first to suggest that [[Magnetohydrodynamics|MHD]] waves in the outer magnetosphere were the sources of oscillations seen at the Earth's surface and that these continuous pulsations were a resonant process<ref>{{Cite encyclopedia |author-last= Kivelson |author-first= M. G.  |title= Pulsations and magnetohydrodynamic wayes |pages= 330–3555 |encyclopedia=Introduction to Space Physics |date= 1995 |publisher=Cambridge University press |isbn=0-521-45104-3 |editor-last1=Kivelson |editor-first1=M. G. |editor-last2=Russell |editor-first2=C. T.  |location=Cambridge U.K.}}</ref> and, in particular he recognised the role of [[Kelvin-Helmholtz wave]]s on magnetospheric boundaries in this context<ref>{{Citation |last=Dungey |first=J. W. |chapter=Instabilities in the Magnetosphere (Theoretical Treatment) |date=1972 |chapter-url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-94-010-3130-1_8 |title=The Magnetosphere |pages=219–235 |editor-last=Dyer |editor-first=E. R. |place=Dordrecht |publisher=Springer Netherlands |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-94-010-3130-1_8 |isbn=978-90-277-0212-8 |access-date=2022-02-26 |editor2-last=Roederer |editor2-first=J. G.|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref> and (with [[David Southwood]]) showed these phenomena gave important  mechanisms and diagnostics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dungey |first1=J. W. |last2=Southwood |first2=D. J. |date=April 1970 |title=Ultra low frequency waves in the magnetosphere |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF00171551 |journal=Space Science Reviews |language=en |volume=10 |issue=5 |page=672 |doi=10.1007/BF00171551 |bibcode=1970SSRv...10..672D |s2cid=123704816 |issn=0038-6308|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Southwood |first1=D. J. |last2=Dungey |first2=J. W. |last3=Etherington |first3=R. J. |date=March 1969 |title=Bounce resonant interaction between pulsations and trapped particles |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0032063369900683 |journal=Planetary and Space Science |language=en |volume=17 |issue=3 |pages=349–361 |doi=10.1016/0032-0633(69)90068-3|bibcode=1969P&SS...17..349S |url-access=subscription }}</ref> He was the first to recognise the importance of magnetosphere-ionosphere coupling<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dungey |first=J. W. |date=1994 |title=Memories, maxims, and motives |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1029/94JA00105 |journal=Journal of Geophysical Research |language=en |volume=99 |issue=A10 |pages=19189–19197 |doi=10.1029/94JA00105 |bibcode=1994JGR....9919189D |issn=0148-0227|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and worked with his student Stephen Knight on the generation of field-aligned potential drops.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Knight |first=S. |date=May 1973 |title=Parallel electric fields |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0032063373900937 |journal=Planetary and Space Science |language=en |volume=21 |issue=5 |pages=741–750 |doi=10.1016/0032-0633(73)90093-7|bibcode=1973P&SS...21..741K |url-access=subscription }}</ref> He proposed [[particle diffusion]] in the [[radiation belt]]s,<ref>{{Citation |last=Dungey |first=J. W. |chapter=The Radiation Belts |date=1964 |chapter-url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/B9780080100036500225 |title=The Planet Earth |pages=311–324 |publisher=Elsevier |language=en |doi=10.1016/b978-0-08-010003-6.50022-5 |isbn=978-0-08-010003-6 |access-date=2022-02-26|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref> and (with [[Stan Cowley]] and Ted Speiser) waves and particles in current sheets.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Robertson |first1=C. |last2=Cowley |first2=S. W. H. |last3=Dungey |first3=J. W. |date=April 1981 |title=Wave-particle interactions in a magnetic neutral sheet |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0032063381900830 |journal=Planetary and Space Science |language=en |volume=29 |issue=4 |pages=399–403 |doi=10.1016/0032-0633(81)90083-0|bibcode=1981P&SS...29..399R |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Dungey was also the first to recognise that gyro-resonant interactions between whistler-mode waves and [[Van Allen radiation belt]] electrons are significant for precipitating the latter into the [[ionosphere]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dungey |first=J. W. |date=June 1963 |title=Loss of van allen electrons due to whistlers |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0032063363901661 |journal=Planetary and Space Science |language=en |volume=11 |issue=6 |pages=591–595 |doi=10.1016/0032-0633(63)90166-1|bibcode=1963P&SS...11..591D |url-access=subscription }}</ref> a mechanism that is fundamental to modern studies of the radiation belts.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Qin |first1=M.|display-authors=etal |date=December 2021 |title=Multi-Point Observations of Modulated Whistler-Mode Waves and Energetic Electron Precipitation |journal=Journal of Geophysical Research: Space Physics |language=en |volume=126 |issue=12|doi=10.1029/2021JA029505|bibcode=2021JGRA..12629505Q|s2cid=245156033|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Dungey also supervised a series of space physicists who went on to make contributions to the field, such as [[David Southwood]], [[Stan Cowley]],<ref name=cowley/> Jeff Hughes,<ref>{{Cite web |last= Professor Jeff Hughes  |title=CV |url=https://www.bu.edu/astronomy/files/2017/09/HughesCV.pdf |access-date=2022-02-28 |website=Boston University|language=en }}</ref> Don Fairfield<ref name=":2"/> and [[Maha Ashour-Abdalla]].{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} He was also a supporter of proposed missions and facilities that were used by the next generation of scientists, such as the European [[Incoherent scatter|Incoherent Scatter]] ([[EISCAT]]) radars and the [[European Space Agency]]'s [[Cluster II (spacecraft)|Cluster]] multi-spacecraft mission. Dungey authored the first proposal for Cluster, calling it TOPS, "Tetrahedral observatory
probe system".<ref>{{Cite encyclopedia |author-last= Taylor |author-first=M.G.G.T.  |title=  The Science of the Cluster Mission |pages= 159–179 |encyclopedia=Magnetospheric Plasma Physics: The Impact of Jim Dungey's Research |date= 2015 |publisher=Springer International Publishing |isbn=978-3-319-18358-9 |editor-last=Cowley |editor-first=S. W. H. |series=Astrophysics and Space Science Proceedings |volume=41 |editor-last2=Southwood |editor-first2=D. J. |editor-last3=Mitton |editor-first3=S.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Souhwood |first1=D. J.|date=June 2013 |title=Jim Dungey at 90 |url=https://academic.oup.com/astrogeo/article/54/3/3.13/211710 |journal=Astronomy and Geophysics |language=en |volume=54 |issue=3 |pages=3.13–3.15 |doi=10.1093/astrogeo/att077|doi-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref> That was in 1966, 30 years before the first attempt to launch Cluster on board the ill-fated [[Ariane flight V88]] of [[Ariane 5]] and 34 years before the spacecraft mission was successfully launched.

=== Awards and honours ===

* 1982 [[Chapman Medal]] from the [[Royal Astronomical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=RAS Chapman Medallists |url=https://ras.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2021-03/Chapman%20Medal_medallists.pdf |website=RAS Chapman medalists}}</ref>
* 1990 [[Gold Medal of the Royal Astronomical Society|Gold Medal]] of the [[Royal Astronomical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=RAS Gold medalists |url=https://ras.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2021-03/Gold%20Medal%202021_0.pdf }}</ref>
* 1991 Fleming Medal from the [[American Geophysical Union]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=James W. Dungey {{!}} |url=https://honors.agu.org/winners/james-w-dungey/ |access-date=2022-02-26 |website=honors.agu.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Anonymous |date=1991 |title=James Dungey receives Fleming Medal |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1029/90EO10239 |journal=Eos, Transactions American Geophysical Union |language=en |volume=72 |issue=29 |pages=309–310 |doi=10.1029/90EO10239 |bibcode=1991EOSTr..72..309. |issn=0096-3941|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 1994 Honorary member of the European Geophysical Society (now the [[European Geosciences Union]]).<ref name=":5" />

The [[James Dungey Lectureship|James Dungey Lecture]] is presented annually in his honour by the [[Royal Astronomical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= Royal Astronomical Society Website |title=James Dungey Lecture |url=https://ras.ac.uk/awards-and-grants/awards/2276-james-dungey-lecture |access-date=2022-02-26 |website=The Royal Astronomical Society |language=en}}</ref>
